t:
(a) Extension of Credit.—Paragraph (2) of section 30C(g) is amended by striking “December 31, 2009” and inserting “December 31, 2010”. 
    (b) Inclusion of Electricity as a Clean-Burning Fuel.—Section 30C(c)(2) is amended by adding at the end the following new subparagraph:“(C) Electricity.”. 
    (c) Effective Date.—The amendments made by this section shall apply to property placed in service after the date of the enactment of this Act, in taxable years ending after such date.

fable.w: This section only extends a tax credit's expiration date, adds electricity as a qualifying clean-burning fuel, and sets an effective date. It contains no consultation, comment period, rulemaking, advisory body, or right to sue involving anyone outside the federal government. The only possible temptation is that taxpayers benefit from the credit, but claiming a tax benefit is not participation in a federal decision.

qwen_block.w: This section amends the Internal Revenue Code to extend a tax credit deadline and include electricity as a qualifying fuel. It does not establish any process for public comment, consultation with outside entities, advisory boards with non-federal members, or rights to sue. It is purely a substantive change to tax law.
qwen_block.s:
(a) Extension of Credit.—Paragraph (2) of section 30C(g) is amended by striking “December 31, 2009” and inserting “December 31, 2010”. 
    (b) Inclusion of Electricity as a Clean-Burning Fuel.—Section 30C(c)(2) is amended by adding at the end the following new subparagraph:“(C) Electricity.”. 
    (c) Effective Date.—The amendments made by this section shall apply to property placed in service after the date of the enactment of this Act, in taxable years ending after such date.

opus.w: This section only extends the deadline for an existing tax credit, adds electricity as a clean-burning fuel, and sets an effective date. It does not require or allow outside parties to be consulted, to comment or to sue over a federal decision, and it gives no agency rulemaking authority. Claiming a tax credit is like applying for a benefit, which the definition excludes.
opus.s: Paragraph (2) of section 30C(g) is amended by striking “December 31, 2009” and inserting “December 31, 2010”.
opus.b: 1. **Tempting reading:** Someone might treat a tax credit that taxpayers claim as a kind of outside involvement in a federal decision. That fails because claiming a credit is like applying for a benefit, which the definition excludes. The section also creates no hearing, comment period, advisory body, consultation, rulemaking authority or right to sue.

qwen_chat.w: This section amends the Internal Revenue Code to extend a credit deadline and include electricity as a clean-burning fuel. It does not establish any mechanism for consultation, coordination, or input from outside parties (such as the public, states, or experts) before the federal government makes a decision. The changes are legislative mandates, not participatory processes.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that amending tax code provisions implicitly involves public participation because tax laws affect the general public. However, the definition requires a specific mechanism for outside parties to consult, coordinate, or provide input *before* a federal decision is made. This section merely changes the text of the law (extending a date and adding a fuel type) without establishing any process for public comment, advisory boards, or consultation with non-federal entities.
